title: How a guy in a bear suit made a tradeshow booth impossible to ignore
summary: Jason Cohen describes using a developer in a panda suit as the Smart Bear tradeshow mascot. The bear drew crowds, created a physical traffic funnel past the booth, and started real conversations because people assumed it was a hired student. A lesson in unconventional, memorable booth tactics, with the bear's calm presence at an awards show getting repeated mentions.

principles.text: Give your tradeshow booth something unmistakable that makes everyone notice and gravitate toward you.
principles.quote: Tradeshow booths need something to help them stand out.  A guy in a bear suit is one way to do it.

principles.text: Position the attention-getter so that even people avoiding it must pass your booth and see your pitch.
principles.quote: if you want to get past the bear you must swing all the way to one side of the aisle (where our booth was) or the other, so (d) you end up getting our pitch and seeing our stuff even if you avoid the bear

principles.text: Put a real expert inside the gimmick; people assume a hired hand, so real product conversations surprise and engage them.
principles.quote: People assume you've hired some poor high school student to stand around in the suit. So when the bear engages you in a discussion of peer code review you might be surprised enough to actually talk about it.

principles.text: Commit fully to the stunt and practice it; the person who wanted to be the bear was great at it.
principles.quote: Roy really wanted to be the bear, and he was really good at it. He spent a lot of time in the bear head back at the office to get used to where the ears and head and eyes and chin were.

principles.text: A crowd around the mascot grows the draw and slows traffic in front of your booth, giving you time to show your stuff and give away a free book.
principles.quote: there was always a crowd around the bear, checking it out, seeing if it could talk, which increases the no-fly zone

principles.text: Calm, deadpan presence beats flailing for attention; acting like it's normal made the bear memorable at an awards show.
principles.quote: He was just calmly sitting there, as if it's normal that a bear would be attending the Jolt Award.
